answer: In an AI-agent market trading copper, voting power is proportional to escrowed stake, not account count, and stake stays locked for 30 days after each vote. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents gives no more power than staking them through one. An oasis of free influence is therefore a fable: to gain more control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital.
